summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an exploratory tool for comparing potential lunar landing areas. We used NASA’s Moon Trek to examine latitude −85.4381°, longitude 37.36667°  and latitude −86.7639°, longitude −22.777°  with LRO Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) topography data. Our prototype presents Our project uses Moon Trek to compare side-by-side terrain views of the two regions so users can visually compare their surface features so users can see how candidate areas differ.

The project addresses the challenge by making lunar terrain information easier to explore and compare. It is important because surface conditions can affect mission planning and landing decisions. This prototype is an educational comparison tool; it does not certify that a location is safe for a real landing.
details:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an educational comparison of two lunar south-pole regions: Nobile Rim 1 and Haworth. We used NASA Moon Trek to view the terrain around each location and present the views together, helping viewers explore how the regions differ. We focused on the locations and terrain information visible in Moon Trek; this project does not calculate a landing-suitability score or certify that either region is safe.

Our goal is to make lunar terrain easier for a general audience to explore and show why surface information matters for mission planning. The creative approach is to compare two candidate regions side by side rather than show a single lunar map. We used NASA Moon Trek and Google Flow to prepare the demonstration video. We did not use custom hardware or coding languages.
